top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a mature, independently reproduced achievement: magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms gave 10^-18 comparisons across several national laboratories and new many-body, gravitational-redshift and fundamental-constant measurements. The two-name allocation is compact and the citation scope is clean, and it is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. I prefer it stand-alone over adding Hosono, since the pairing has no common thread, although Hosono's discovery is verified and cleanly attributed, so P002 is acceptable and clearly better than no award.
